newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil state opens lone bid on hydropower project.
newsitem.headline: Brazil state opens lone bid on hydropower project.

text.p: A U.S.-Brazilian group has offered Rio Grande do Sul state five to 15 percent of energy output over 30 years for a contract to build and run a hydropower plant in southern Brazil, an official said.
A state spokeswoman said the lone bid, cast on January 17 by a consortium including U.S.-based Alcoa Aluminio, was opened on Thursday by Rio Grande do Sul energy officials.
The group offered five percent of production over the first 10 years; 10 percent in the second decade and 15 percent in the third for the 125-megawatt Dona Francisca project.
The consortium also said the facility would cost 137 million reais ($131 million) and take 46 months to build.

The state plans to name the winning bidder and award the contract by mid-February. Apart from Alcoa, the consortium also includes local firms Camargo Correa Industrias, Inepar and Centrais Eletricas Santa Catarina and units of Brazilian groups Gerdau and Votorantim.

The Dona Francisca plant will be built on the Jacui River, about 217 miles (350 kms) from state capital Porto Alegre and will include two 62.5 MW turbines and tie into the state's power grid. It will create 600 to 700 jobs and provide four percent of the state's energy needs, the spokeswoman said.
